## Purpose and entry points
Carbon is an open-core, API-first manufacturing platform spanning ERP, MES, QMS, MRP, traceability, accounting, and integrations. The primary user-facing applications are React Router/TypeScript apps: ERP administration and business workflows, MES shop-floor execution, Academy training, and a starter API consumer. Application bootstraps are `apps/erp/app/entry.server.tsx`, `apps/mes/app/entry.server.tsx`, and `apps/academy/app/entry.server.tsx`; route registries and nested route handlers provide both UI and server actions.

## ERP application and domain-module boundary
`apps/erp` is the principal business application. Its module folders follow a recurring boundary: data models/server operations/services, typed domain interfaces, and UI; routes compose those modules into authenticated `/x` workflows, public/auth flows, file rendering, and APIs. The largest domain areas are sales/purchasing documents, items/revisions/methods, inventory, production, quality, accounting, resources, settings, and workflows. This is a modular monolith rather than separate domain services.
Paths: `apps/erp/app/modules/sales/sales.service.ts`, `apps/erp/app/modules/production/production.service.ts`, `apps/erp/app/routes/x+/`.

## Manufacturing lifecycle and shared system of record
Item master data, revisions, bills of material, and make methods drive quoting, sales orders, purchasing, jobs, inventory movements, scheduling, and shop-floor operations. Inventory preserves lot/serial tracked entities and lineage; production jobs expose operation dependency DAGs and capacity-aware scheduling; quality inspections/nonconformances can disposition material. Financial posting is a cross-cutting boundary: inventory, receipts, shipments, invoices, payments, and job completion feed journals, periods, reports, and accounting synchronization.
Paths: `apps/erp/app/modules/items/items.models.ts`, `apps/erp/app/modules/inventory/inventory.service.ts`, `apps/erp/app/modules/accounting/accounting.models.ts`.

## MES execution surface
`apps/mes` is a separate shop-floor client sharing identity and the underlying Carbon database. Operators work assigned/active operations, execute steps, issue or consume material, record quantities, inspections, scrap/rework, timecards, picking, maintenance, and work-center displays. MES-specific server services encapsulate execution behavior, while route actions update shared production/inventory/quality records. ERP and MES therefore converge at the database and business-event boundaries rather than calling each other’s UI.
Paths: `apps/mes/app/services/operations.service.ts`, `apps/mes/app/services/inventory.service.ts`, `apps/mes/app/components/JobOperation/JobOperation.tsx`.

## Database, security, and API boundary
Supabase/Postgres is the authoritative persistence, auth, storage, realtime, and RLS layer. Its migration history defines the multi-tenant company/group schema, ABAC/RBAC permissions, views, triggers, posting behavior, and database RPCs. `@carbon/auth` centralizes sessions, MFA, passkeys, API keys, and company authorization. External clients may use Supabase directly with API keys, or use the ERP’s versioned ORPC/OpenAPI and MCP surfaces.
Paths: `packages/database/supabase/migrations/`, `packages/auth/src/services/auth.server.ts`, `apps/erp/app/routes/api+/v1+/$.ts`.

## Asynchronous automation and workflows
Inngest provides the durable asynchronous control plane for integration sync, notifications, document extraction, backups/restores, MRP and replanning, model processing, printing, and scheduled maintenance. Database/application events are queued and fan out into these workers. A user-configurable workflow subsystem has three layers: shared definition/catalog/runtime semantics, ERP visual builder/run history, and job-side execution/actions; this isolates workflow authoring from execution.
Paths: `packages/jobs/src/inngest/functions/`, `packages/workflows/src/definition/schema.ts`, `packages/jobs/src/workflows/engine/execute.ts`.

## Geometry and 3D pipeline
The optional Rust assembler service converts STEP/CAD data to GLB/XBF-like artifacts, optimizes meshes, and plans assembly motion using OpenCASCADE, FCL collision support, Draco, and internal planner crates. ERP uploads and monitors model artifacts; Inngest task workers call the service and persist results. The viewer package renders optimized/raw models, assembly steps, motion paths, and planning output.
Paths: `apps/assembler/src/main.rs`, `crates/planner/src/pipeline.rs`, `packages/viewer/src/AssemblyViewer.tsx`.

## Infrastructure and external integrations
Local development is orchestrated per worktree by `crbn`, which launches Dockerized Postgres/Supabase services, Redis, Inngest, mail capture, and edge runtime; SST/Vercel-oriented configuration supports deployment. Redis backs rate limiting/cache/lockout behavior. Integration adapters cover accounting providers (QuickBooks, Xero, Rillet), Stripe/Stripe Connect, Onshape CAD, Jira, Linear, Slack, Paperless Parts, SMTP/Resend, and OpenAI-backed embeddings/agent capabilities.
Paths: `packages/dev/docker/docker-compose.dev.yml`, `packages/ee/src/accounting/core/sync.ts`, `packages/jobs/src/inngest/functions/integrations/`.
